extracted.intended_audience: authors/researchers submitting preprints to arXiv (registered authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical requirements for preparing and submitting an article to arXiv, including permitted file formats, figure handling, metadata, and announcement timing. Covers responsibilities of submitters and how to edit/replace submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only registered arXiv users may submit. Use the Submit form or 'START NEW SUBMISSION' from your user page.

rubrics_metrics.name: License / distribution rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must ensure you have the right to grant distribution; choose or confirm an appropriate license during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to arXiv terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must agree to arXiv terms of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with arXiv terms is required as part of the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: No submissions with omitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions missing essential content are rejected because they are unhelpful to readers and of limited archival value. Do not submit partial/placeholder files or abstracts alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted text formats and preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ArXiv's goal is to store portable/stable formats; (La)TeX is preferred because it does not hide information. Note arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source. Word-processor users should save as PDF. Scanned documents are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on scanned documents
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv will not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not scan papers (e.g., as images embedded in PDFs); produce proper electronic source or PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures can be in PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG, GIF, PNG, or PDF (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate formats: PS/EPS for line drawings/plots, JPEG for photos, GIF/PNG for bitmaps. If including PDF figures, only use them with PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size and accessibility considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections may not be able to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce figure size as much as possible; arXiv provides information on submission sizes and bitmapping. Large figures should still be included (do not omit) but optimized. Contact arXiv administrators if you have problems with a large submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No external-only figure hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures even if you provide a link to another server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures that are part of the article must be included in the submission package; external links do not substitute for included figure files.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX figure inclusion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard, widely-supported LaTeX packages so arXiv processing can render figures. arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues—seek help from colleagues if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other character (e.g., spaces, question marks, asterisks) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. Follow these restrictions to ensure portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case sensitivity of file names and internal references
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on arXiv; e.g., 'Figure1.PDF' and 'figure1.pdf' are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal file references (such as LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match case exactly regardless of your local OS's case sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) which are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files for accepted practices and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare separate title/abstract information used on abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate instructions on title/abstract preparation to ensure metadata is suitable for discovery and announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read arXiv messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the final 'Submit Article' step, check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or formatting issues, correct them or contact arXiv administrators. You can 'Unsubmit' an article before public announcement to return it to incomplete status and modify it; Unsubmitting removes it from the processing queue and announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing/replacing vs. resubmitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed. Edits and final submission before 14:00 US Eastern Time Monday–Friday will not delay announcement. Authors are encouraged to update and correct articles via replacement, not by creating new submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make their own submissions; third-party submissions (e.g., by secretaries) are discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions are often the ones that cause the most problems. Ensure the submitting author takes responsibility and supplies required information (institutional affiliation and official report numbers from the author's institution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided; official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate affiliation and any institutional report numbers in the metadata during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and announcement timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All official versions of submitted articles are made publicly available; submissions to arXiv are normally made public on Sunday through Thursday, with no announcements Friday or Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the announcement schedule and 'freeze' times: submissions received between certain 24-hour windows are announced the same evening (20:00 US Eastern) of the next day as specified in the availability table. See the availability/announcement order discussion (policy change 2017-01) for exact timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit an article, use the Submit form or select 'START NEW SUBMISSION' from your user page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online submission workflow; check the availability of new submissions as explained in the availability section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for accessibility issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a disability and are having trouble accessing information or need materials in an alternate format, contact web-accessibility@cornell.edu for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this contact for accessibility-related help with the arXiv website or submission materials.
